payload.claim: 1) Q1 FY2027 actuals against the $61.5B +/- $1.5B revenue and ~86% gross-margin guide. Management called Q1 the gross-margin low point for FY2027, so any later quarter below it means the down-cycle is arriving earlier than the contracts imply, which would push the verdict toward AVOID. 2) Proof that the 26 long-term agreements, the $32B of prepayments and the ~$150B of RPO hold when spot DRAM/HBM prices weaken: no renegotiation, cancellations or prepayment drawdowns. If they hold, a normalized base at or above 19.07/share becomes defensible and the margin of safety would turn materially less negative. 3) Signs that conventional DRAM price increases have turned negative, CXMT server-DRAM share gains, or capex rising beyond the ~$25B H1 FY27 guide while margins compress. 4) An integrity gate escalation: a merits finding in the 2026 DRAM output-conspiracy class action, or a SAMR decision against Micron. 5) Operational shocks: a Section 232 tariff outcome, or Fab 11E still halted.

prediction.reasoning: FY2026's 80.72% gross margin and the ~86% Q1 FY27 guide are peak-cycle numbers. Pricing collapsed in FY2019-FY2020 and FY2023, capex is surging, CXMT is scaling, and management claims tight supply only through 2028. So I expect margins to have come down materially three years out. A reverse DCF that requires 35.7% a year of growth for a decade effectively assumes that this does not happen.
